Codex, thanks for restating the shape of things, but I want to push back hard on one specific line in your message: "Background Fetch: If needed, configure background fetch to periodically update due dates without user interaction." That's not a minor detail to leave as "if needed" — it's actively wrong for this app and I want it dead in this round, not carried forward as an ambiguous maybe. Due-dates aren't something that needs updating in the background at all; they're computed live, on demand, from the shared due function whenever a screen appears. There's nothing to "keep fresh" via BGTaskScheduler because nothing is ever stale — that's the entire point of computing due-ness at display-time instead of caching it. Adding background fetch here would mean requesting a capability with zero actual use, which is exactly the kind of scope-creep-by-default-Xcode-template thing that trips up App Review ("why does an offline flashcard app have Background Modes enabled?") and adds an attack surface and battery cost for a feature that doesn't exist. I want this locked explicitly: Background Modes capability stays unchecked in the target, full stop, no background fetch, no silent push, nothing. Same note on your "ensure users grant permission... crucial for timely review prompts" line — that's flipped from what's actually locked. Reminders are optional and denial has to be handled gracefully with zero degradation to core function (DEC-prompt_contract-004); "crucial" language is the wrong frame for a feature that must work identically whether the user grants it or not.

On the stuff you did agree with — SwiftData for persistence, batch fetching, snapshot handling — I don't think there's daylight between us, but I noticed nobody has actually pushed back on any of the nine specific things I put on the table last round: the RecallCore-as-real-SPM-package boundary, Clock injection, raw Int/Bool instead of enums for predicate-filterable fields, the @Attribute(.unique)-vs-CloudKit conflict, synchronous context.save() on every grade, an automated XCUITest for the force-quit case instead of a manual checklist item, scenePhase-based permission re-polling, the EntitlementGate abstraction for deferred StoreKit, and the CSV non-UTF8/large-file rules. There's no ML use case anywhere in this app's locked feature set — no OCR, no handwriting recognition, no personalization model, no AR flashcard visualization — and I want to close that off explicitly rather than let it sit unaddressed: zero ML/Vision/CoreML/ARKit surface in this app, and if anyone later proposes something like "auto-generate cards from a photo," that's new scope requiring its own justification pass, not something to sneak in under "polish." I also want to sharpen the CSV size cap slightly rather than leave "roughly 20,000 rows" sitting as a rough number — let's make it exact: 10,000 rows as the hard cap for a single import file, chosen because it's comfortably above what a real single-deck export would ever contain (even a serious language learner's deck runs a few thousand cards, not tens of thousands) while still being small enough that a streamed, chunked parse finishes in well under a second on-device — no spinner needed, no async preview-loading state to design for. **SwiftUI architecture:** MV over ceremony-heavy MVVM — views hold `@Environment(\.modelContext)` for direct CRUD, but review-queue construction and stats aggregation go through two dedicated `@Observable` services, `DueQueryService` and `SessionEngine`, so the project's standing "one shared function, never reimplemented per screen" rule is enforced by there being exactly one type, not by convention.

**Core module boundary:** `RecallCore` ships as a real local Swift Package (not a folder group) containing the pure SM-2 engine, the shared due-computation function, and the RFC4180 CSV parser/writer, operating on plain structs with zero import of SwiftData or SwiftUI. Every function that needs "now" takes an injected `Clock` protocol (a `SystemClock` default, a `TestClock` for tests), which makes DST and calendar-day-boundary unit tests deterministic on CI regardless of machine time zone, independent of and in addition to the simulator-clock-jump integration test already locked for app-level wiring.

**Data model:** grade and demo-flag fields are stored as raw `Int`/`Bool`, never Swift enums with associated values, because SwiftData's `#Predicate` macro can't reliably filter those — modeling them as enums would silently force a fallback to the already-banned post-fetch filtering. No `@Attribute(.unique)` anywhere in the schema, since it's incompatible with the CloudKit-shaped-schema requirement locked in an earlier phase.

**Persistence guarantee:** every grade write calls `context.save()` synchronously — autosave timing is not trusted for this. The force-quit/relaunch guarantee is verified by a real automated XCUITest that actually terminates and relaunches the app, not a manual checklist step.

**Permissions/privacy:** the notification-permission toggle re-polls real `UNUserNotificationCenter` state on every `scenePhase` transition to `.active`, never caching the original grant. Background Modes capability stays fully unchecked in the target — no background fetch, no silent push, nothing — since due-ness is always computed live at display time and there is nothing to keep "fresh." A `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` manifest declaring zero data collection is required.

**StoreKit:** stays deferred (should-have, per the earlier app_features decision), but every entitlement/cap check routes through one `EntitlementGate` service that reports unlimited today, so real billing is additive later, not a rewrite.

**CSV:** non-UTF8 files are rejected outright with one clear error rather than guessing an encoding; single-file import is hard-capped at exactly 10,000 rows with a plain-language "check you selected the right file" error above that, parsed off the main actor via streaming.

**ML/AR:** zero surface for either. No OCR, no personalization model, no CoreML, no ARKit — nothing in the locked six core features calls for it, and any future proposal along those lines is new scope requiring its own justification pass.
